config.name: erag_pilot
config.description: The five GPT-OSS-120B systems of the EnterpriseRAG-Bench pilot (50 questions, 10,000-document slice), their saved answers scored with the 4Minds RAG metrics. The scorer config (configs/scorers/) gives the judge.

metric_notes.deepeval_hallucination: Context is the gold facts, one item per fact. Score = facts with the verdict 'agrees' / all facts (higher is better). The prompt forgives missing detail, but the judges often give 'does not agree' to a non-answer, so 'I don't know' usually scores 0.

anthropic-claude-haiku-5-5-nothink: Haiku judge: the Anthropic OpenAI-compatible endpoint rejects the RAGAS response_format {"type": "json_object"} (HTTP 400), so the scorer config removes that field (drop_params). The prompt with the JSON schema is the same; Haiku puts the JSON in a code fence, which the scorer removes before parsing (about 340 fences per system). gpt-4o-mini got the field.

Haiku judge: the first pass hit the rate limit of 80,000 output tokens per minute (HTTP 429) at 16 parallel requests; two retry passes, the same for every system, scored all such items. 4 items stay not scored, and they are not in the means: Summarization of qst_0454 for LangChain, RAGFlow and GraphRAG (the answer is only a date, and Haiku replied in prose that the text to extract claims from was empty; audit step diagnose_v2_qst_0454), and Factual Correctness of qst_0433 for RAGFlow (the claim list was longer than the 4,096-token limit).

systems.name: 4Minds (Constellations)
systems.description: 4Minds prod, Constellations engine (WebSocket), GPT-OSS-120B served by 4Minds; one file per document

ingestion.cost_covers: not known: 4Minds runs the ETL, embeddings and graph build on its servers and does not report a cost
ingestion.note: The time counts from the restart of the wait (21:36 UTC). The upload started at 21:22 UTC and the chunk count did not change after 21:39 UTC, so the ingestion itself took about 17 minutes.

caveats: 4Minds: the document IDs come from the chunk document_title (file name <dsid>_<title>.txt), in chunk score order.

systems.name: GPT-OSS + LangChain
systems.description: LangChain TokenTextSplitter (512 tokens, 10% overlap), text-embedding-3-large, FAISS; 100 chunks to the top 10 full documents; the official answer prompt; GPT-OSS-120B on Amazon Bedrock

ingestion.ran_on: operator's Mac (FAISS index); embeddings on the OpenAI API

caveats: LangChain: always gives 10 documents, so its document precision is at most 0.1 for a question with one gold document.

systems.name: GPT-OSS + GraphRAG
systems.description: Microsoft GraphRAG 3.3.0, fast indexing method with default settings, local search (community level 2), text-embedding-3-large; GPT-OSS-120B on Amazon Bedrock
systems.short: Microsoft GraphRAG, fast method, local search

ingestion.cost_covers: GPT-OSS-120B on Bedrock (16,173 calls) and embeddings (29.1 M tokens)
ingestion.note: The build stopped once in its last step (the OpenAI account had no credits); that step ran again from the GraphRAG cache. The time is the sum of the two runs, without the wait.

caveats: GraphRAG: this row is not representative of GraphRAG. The fast method writes no entity descriptions, so local search compares the question only with entity names. On a 500-document test, the standard method found 52 of 74 gold documents and the fast method 17 of 74 (see the EnterpriseRAG-Bench run README).

systems.name: GPT-OSS + RAGFlow
systems.description: RAGFlow v0.27.2 (self-hosted), naive chunking (512 tokens), text-embedding-3-large; the retrieval API with the default chat-assistant settings (6 chunks, hybrid search); GPT-OSS-120B on Amazon Bedrock

ingestion.cost_covers: embeddings (text-embedding-3-large, 12.5 M tokens as RAGFlow counts them)
ingestion.ran_on: operator's Windows PC (Docker in WSL2, CPU parsing); embeddings on the OpenAI API
ingestion.note: Upload 281 s and parse 8,385 s. The parse time depends on the CPU of that PC.

systems.name: GPT-OSS, no RAG
systems.description: GPT-OSS-120B on Amazon Bedrock with the official answer prompt and an empty Context Documents section (world-knowledge baseline)
caveats: No RAG: the system gets no documents, so all its document scores are 0 by design. It has 49 answers; the question without an answer is not scored.

Pilot: 50 of 500 EnterpriseRAG-Bench questions, stratified by question type (2 to 17 per type), on a 10,000-document corpus slice. The judge is not fully repeatable. Do not rank systems from small differences.

Not an official protocol: these are 4Minds RAG metrics on the saved answers of the EnterpriseRAG-Bench run. The systems did not answer again. The references are the EnterpriseRAG-Bench gold answer (Answer Accuracy, Factual Correctness), gold facts (Summarization, Hallucination) and gold documents (document retrieval).

Summarization: the 'original text' is the gold facts of the question, not the retrieved context. The score shows how well the answer covers the gold facts (coverage) without statements that the facts do not support (alignment); score = min(alignment, coverage).

Hallucination: DeepEval checks the answer against each gold fact. The score is the fraction of facts with the verdict 'agrees' (higher is better). The DeepEval prompt says that missing detail is not a contradiction, but the judges often give 'does not agree' to an answer that says the documents do not have the information; so a non-answer scores 0 for most questions and 1 for some (No RAG has 27 non-answers: 22 score 0 with gpt-4o-mini, 18 with Haiku). Read it together with Answer Accuracy and Factual Correctness. (The note in the scorer configs says that 'I don't know' scores 1; that is the intent of the prompt, not what the judges did.)

Two kinds of precision, recall and F1: Factual Correctness counts claims (claims of the answer supported by the gold answer, and claims of the gold answer found in the answer; judge). Document retrieval counts document IDs (the documents the system gave against the gold documents; no judge, exact match).

Document retrieval uses the original gold documents (no correction step, unlike the official EnterpriseRAG-Bench scorer) and only the 46 questions that have gold documents. Systems that give many documents get a lower precision.

config.name: v2_haiku-nothink
config.description: 4Minds RAG v2: the metrics of v1 with the same settings; only the judge is different. Judge: Claude Haiku 5.5 with thinking disabled.

judge.note: The backend entry removes temperature and top_p (Haiku 5.5 rejects them) and disables thinking. drop_params also removes the RAGAS response_format {"type": "json_object"}: the Anthropic OpenAI-compatible endpoint accepts only json_schema (HTTP 400). The JSON schema instructions of the RAGAS prompt stay; the code fence around the JSON is removed before parsing.

metrics.label: Answer Accuracy (RAGAS, NVIDIA)
metrics.note: The question and the answer against the gold answer; two judge ratings (0, 2 or 4), each with the roles swapped, scaled to 0-1 and averaged.

metrics.label: Factual Correctness (RAGAS)
metrics.note: Claims of the answer checked against the gold answer (precision) and claims of the gold answer checked against the answer (recall); F1 from the same TP, FP and FN, with the formulas of FactualCorrectness.

metrics.label: Summarization (DeepEval)
metrics.note: The original text is the gold facts of the question, the same for every system. The 5 assessment questions are made once per question by `pipeline/score_extra.py prepare` and used for every system. Score = min(alignment, coverage).

metrics.label: Hallucination (DeepEval; higher is better)
metrics.note: Context is the gold facts, one context item per fact. The score is the fraction of facts that the answer does not contradict, so "I don't know" scores 1.

metrics.label: Document retrieval (no judge)
metrics.note: The document IDs that the system gave against the original gold document IDs (no correction); only questions with gold documents. Precision is 0 when the system gave no documents.
